evidence.intree_statement: Class AUniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) (a : D) := { universal_arrow : c ~> fobj[F] a ; universal_arrow_universal {d} {f : c ~> (fobj[F] d)} : Unique (fun g : hom a d => fmap[F] g ∘ universal_arrow ≈ f) }.

Class UniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) := { arrow_initial : @Initial (=(c) ↓ F); arrow_obj := snd (`1 (@initial_obj _ arrow_initial)); arrow : c ~> F arrow_obj := `2 (@initial_obj _ arrow_initial) }.
Corollary ump_universal_arrows `(c ⟿ F) `(h : c ~> F d) : ∃! g : arrow_obj ~> d, h ≈ fmap[F] g ∘ arrow.

statement_record.book: Given S : D -> C and c in C, a universal arrow from c to S is a pair <r, u : c -> S r> such that every f : c -> S d factors as S f' o u = f for a unique f' : r -> d.
statement_record.intree: Class AUniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) (a : D) := { universal_arrow : c ~> fobj[F] a ; universal_arrow_universal : Unique (fun g : hom a d => fmap[F] g ∘ universal_arrow ≈ f) } — plus the equivalent comma-initial packaging UniversalArrow with derived ump_universal_arrows.

statement_record.book: Two-way subsumption: (a) a universal element <r, e> of H : D -> Set is exactly a universal arrow from the one-point set * to H; (b) when C has small hom-sets, <r, u> is a universal arrow from c to S iff <r, u> is a universal element of the functor H = C(c, S -) : D -> Set.
statement_record.intree: UniversalArrowIsUniversalProperty: universal arrows from c to U correspond to representations of d ↦ Hom_C(c, U d); representability_by_yoneda: universal elements correspond to representations. Composing the two isomorphisms yields direction (b); the book's small-hom-sets hypothesis is automatic (hom-setoids of any category land in Sets).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: both correspondences route through representations and their composite (universal arrow ⟺ universal element of Hom_C(c, U ─)) is not stated as a single theorem; the one-point-set formulation (a) is entirely absent. Where in force, no extra hypotheses — smallness is free in the setoid setting

gap: Half (a) — a universal element of H : D -> Set is the same as a universal arrow from the one-point set * to H — has no counterpart (no mediation through global elements */terminal setoid; grep -rniE 'one.point|singleton set' over *.v finds no such bridge; Instance/One.v is the terminal CATEGORY, not the one-point setoid trick).
